subject: Ethiopian wolf
title: These Monkeys Let a Wolf Walk Right Through Their Herd

scenes.text: A wolf walks into a herd of monkeys. The monkeys keep eating.
In Ethiopia's highlands, gelada monkeys graze in herds of up to a thousand.
When a lone Ethiopian wolf strolls in, two thirds of the time they barely move.
Domestic dogs get a very different reaction. The monkeys flee to the cliffs.
The wolf isn't after them. It hunts the rats hiding under the grazing herd.
Among the monkeys, it catches its rat two times in three. Alone, one in four. So the wolf leaves the babies alone.

description:
A lone Ethiopian wolf can walk into a herd of gelada monkeys, and most of the time the monkeys do not even move.
A 2015 study on Ethiopia's Guassa Plateau found wolves caught rodents in 67% of attempts among gelada herds, against 25% when hunting alone, and they passed up chances to attack young geladas.
Why do you think the herd helps the wolf?
thumbnail_text: A WOLF INSIDE A MONKEY HERD
first_comment: Fewer than 500 Ethiopian wolves are left in the wild. Would you trust a wolf in your herd?
